prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: replacement cloud-floor painting for the top-down 2D game Silken Hell.
Edit target: Image 1, the existing full-coverage cloud floor.
Style references: Image 2 shows world 1 in the actual game: match its quiet matte ground, restrained contrast and fine illustrative material. Image 3 is a foreground bird sprite, only a reference for the game's ivory/slate palette, not a subject to include.
Primary request: redraw the cloud floor as a beautiful, calm, hand-painted sea of ROUND flowing clouds, viewed directly from above. Eliminate the very busy dithering and repetitive little bumps of image 1. Use large graceful asymmetrical cloud banks with rounded scalloped silhouettes, some small curling wisps, delicately drawn pale crests and soft slate-blue shadow pockets underneath. Cloud shapes overlap naturally with varied sizes and curved silhouettes. Let the main surfaces breathe with quiet areas, a very subtle gouache grain and very few contour accents. The material should sit underneath the small dark pixel-art characters without competing with them.
Palette: muted dusty blue-grey shadows, pearl grey and warm ivory cloud tops; gentle diffuse light from upper left. Clearly illustrated 2D game art with elegant clean soft-edged drawing, not photographic clouds.
Composition: continuous full-bleed cloud floor, even distributed detail, no central focal point, overhead view, landscape image. All cloud masses feel round and airy. Retain opaque coverage.
Avoid: square tiles, cubes, faceted polygons, grid alignment, voxel art, coarse pixel blocks, blurry airbrush blobs, noise-heavy dithering, hard black outlines, strong contrast, 3D render, horizon, distant perspective, buildings, sky openings, black holes, characters, UI, borders, frames, text or logos.
